project.title: Microbial compartmentalization reveals overlapping nitrogen transformation pathways in an intermittently aerated structured-bed hybrid bioreactor treating dairy wastewater
project.description: Intermittently aerated biofilm systems have emergedas promising alternatives for biological nitrogen removal under lowcarbon-to-nitrogen ratio conditions. However, the relationships between reactorperformance, microbial compartmentalization, and functional organization withinstructured hybrid systems have not yet been fully elucidated. In this study, a laboratory-scalestructured-bed hybrid baffled reactor (SBHBR) treating dairy wastewater wasoperated for 250 days under different hydraulic retention times (36 h and 48 h) and intermittent aerationstrategies across five operational phases to investigate how microbialcompartmentalization influences carbon and nitrogen transformation pathwayswithin the reactor. The reactor consisted of anaerobic (C1-C3) andoxic/anoxic (C4-C5) compartments containing polyurethane foam support media.Physicochemical monitoring was integrated with 16S rRNA gene sequencing,microbial network analysis, redundancy analysis, and predictive functionalprofiling. The SBHBR maintained high COD removal efficiencies (>96%)throughout the experimental period, while total nitrogen removal exceeded 35%under all operational conditions and reached 82.4% during the optimized phase.Microbial analyses revealed a clear spatial compartmentalization, with methanogenicand fermentative populations predominating in the anaerobic compartments,whereas genera potentially involved in nitrogen transformation, including Acinetobacter,Pseudomonas, and Limnobacter, were enriched in the intermittently aerated compartments. Functional predictions indicated that anaerobic digestion represented the dominant metabolic process within the system, while nitrification- and denitrification-related pathways were primarily associated with the oxic/anoxic zone. These findings demonstrate that intermittent aeration combined with reactor compartmentalization promotes complementary microbial functions, enabling stable carbon conversion and efficient nitrogen removal under low COD/TN conditions. The integration of operational and microbial analyses provides valuable insights for the optimization and scale-up of energy-efficient hybrid biofilm reactors for dairy wastewater treatment.
